011b0e34817dd296.summary: Banks report annual cash deposits of ₹10L+ to Income Tax under SFT rules, while direct family gifts have no upper limit. Hook: 'Why depositing ₹10 lakh in cash gets an IT notice, but a ₹50 lakh gift from parents is 100% tax-free.'
011b0e34817dd296.notes:
- Cash deposits exceeding ₹10 lakh in savings accounts or ₹50 lakh in current accounts in a financial year trigger automated Statement of Financial Transactions (SFT) reporting by banks to the IT Department.
- Section 56(2)(x) exemptions: gifts from specified relatives (parents, spouse, siblings, lineal ascendants/descendants) are completely exempt from income tax with no upper threshold.
- Key documentation required: gift deed, bank transfer proof (never cash), and donor source of funds justification.
- High-value cash deposits without clear withdrawal trails trigger Section 68/69 unexplained money notices taxed at 78% effective rate.
